To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

half-anther culture in A. andreanum cv. ‘Tropik’ was successfully improved by using an optimized isolation technique (adaxial side down) and by culturing half anthers on WT medium supplemented 0.5 mg/l 2, 4-D in combination of 0.01 mg/l NAA, and 1 mg/l BA and 1.5 g/l Gelrite.
callus induction and plant regeneration from half-anthers of Anthurium were successfully improved through optimization of isolation technique and initiation medium.

callus formation in half-anther cultures of Anthurium was significantly influenced by isolation technique and initiation medium, and the most effective medium was WT medium with 0.05 mg/l N6-benzylaminopurine (BA), 0.5–1.0 g/1 Gelrite, and 0.1–0.5 % activated charcoal.

the development of a reliable protocol for the production of anthurium plantlets via half-anther culture.
the improvement of callus formation from anthurium half anthers and the optimization of the initiation culture medium for callus induction and plant regeneration.
the optimization of the initiation culture medium and isolation technique of half anthers in Anthurium andrewanum cv. ‘Tropica’.

callus induction and plantlet regeneration in Anthurum andreanum cv. ‘Tropik’ was improved by optimizing the isolation technique and the initiation culture medium.

the best callus formation was obtained when the half-anthers were placed on the WT medium supplemented with the 2,4 D (0.5 μM) and the NAA (0.01 μM) with the BA (1.0 μM) in combination with the TDZ (0.5 μM), using the Gelrite (1.5 %).
the best medium for callus initiation in half-anther cultures of Anthurium is WT medium with 1.5-g/l Gelrite supplemented with 0,01 mg/l 0,5 mg/l NNA and 2,4D and 1.0-0.5 mg/l BA and TDZ.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the best protocol for Anthurium half-anther callus induction is as follows: half-anthers cultured abaxial-side down for 2 weeks on WT medium supplemented 0.5–1.0 g Gelrite, then transferred to the same medium supplemented with 1.5–2.0 mg Gelrite for 2 months, and finally transferred onto NWT medium supplemented with 2.5 g Gelrite for shoot multiplication and rooting.
the isolation technique, medium composition and gelling agents are critical for callus induction in half-anther cultures of Anthurium.
the half-anther culture protocol for Anthurium is now ready for application in breeding programs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the isolation technique of half anthers is a critical factor that can affect the success of callus induction and that a suitable medium is needed to induce the growth of half anthers.
half-anthers should be cultured abaxial-side down to improve the callus induction rate, and that the addition of 2,4- D to the initiation culture medium enhances callus induction and growth.
the adaxial surface is the best surface to culture half-anthers on, and that the addition of 0.01–0.5 μM of 2,4- D to WT medium can improve callus induction.
